scope: Bounded exact primary-source comparison. Exact passport existence has established precedent; fullA_n follows from prior results for even n>=10. Explicit coefficient family and braid-orbit priority remain separate.
assurance: Internal source statement/application checking. No independent reproof of imported theorems, external review, or exhaustive worldwide priority search.

sources.title: Realizability of branched coverings of surfaces
sources.version: Transactions of the American Mathematical Society 282 no.2 (April1984),773-790
sources.statement: A branch datum containing(d-1,1) is realizable iff its total defect is even and at least2d-2, excluding the two listed exceptional families.
sources.application: Our n=2b>=8,q=b+1>=5 passport has defect2n-2 and avoids both exceptions; hence it is already realizable.
sources.reading_limits: Read statement and its reduction proof; no independent proof of all preliminary permutation lemmas.

sources.title: Solution of the Hurwitz problem for Laurent polynomials
sources.version: Journal of Knot Theory and Its Ramifications18 no.2 (2009),271-302; accepted31August2007
sources.statement: Every genus-zero Laurent passport with more than three branch values is realizable.
sources.application: Exact passport DT^b,(2b-1,1) has b+1>=5 values and a length-two partition; it is a direct specialization.
sources.reading_limits: Read definitions and theorem; inspected proof architecture and final deduction inSection3. Does not prescribe arithmetic field, geometric group, or a particular tuple.

sources.title: Characteristically simple Beauville groups, I: cartesian powers of alternating groups
sources.statement: A primitive finite permutation group of degree n>=9 containing a double transposition contains A_n.
sources.application: For even n>=10, any transitive realization of our passport is primitive by its(n-1)-cycle and all branch cycles are even, hence its group equalsA_n.
sources.reading_limits: Jones imports the classical small-support result and cites Cameron's proof sketch. This audit imports that exact theorem; no independent reproof of its classification.

sources.title: The monodromy group of a function on a general curve
sources.statement: For each n>=6 there exist fullA_n genus-zero covers with all n-1 branch cycles double transpositions.
sources.application: Shows prior genus-zero DT alternating covers; does not prescribe the long-cycle(n-1,1) pole fiber.
sources.reading_limits: Read exact genus-zero statement and degree-raising proof; its n6 base delegates to GAP/direct check, not independently replayed here.

sources.title: Alternating groups as monodromy groups in positive characteristic
sources.statement: Alternating covers of generic curves with all3-cycle or allDT inertia in the exact characteristic and degree ranges stated.
sources.application: Related prescribed-ramification covers; not a statement about a single long(n-1)-cycle or denominatorz.
sources.reading_limits: Read the listed theorem statements and genus-zero construction. Positive-characteristic ranges are not extended to unlisted cases.

sources.title: Constructions polynomiales et theorie de Galois
sources.statement: For odd n and general rationalP, constructs rationalQ,R with P'Q-PQ'=R², and Disc(P-tQ)=Disc(P)S(t)²; branch specializations have one triple root.
sources.application: Prior square-discriminant pencil mechanism with general denominator and3-cycle branching, distinct from paired simple critical points of our fixedlinear-denominator pencil.
sources.reading_limits: Read construction and proof explanation; this comparison does not assert rational descent of the DT passport.

sources.title: Permutation groups with a cyclic two-orbits subgroup and monodromy groups of Laurent polynomials
sources.statement: Natural alternating/symmetric monodromy is retained with many ramification possibilities in the indecomposable two-pole classification.
sources.application: Does not certify a particular passport or arithmetic field; more exact realizability precedent is EKS1984 and Pakovich2009.
sources.reading_limits: Reused existing retained PDF; no change to the earlier ledger or source.
